$comment: Copy to <repo>/.cursor/hooks.json (merge if one exists). Assumes the pack is vendored at .harness/. Cursor honors exit code 2 = deny, so the portable policies' exit codes flow straight through run-hook.sh; failClosed:true blocks on unexpected hook failure. `stop` goes through cursor/stop-gate.sh because Cursor continues via {followup_message}, not an exit code. `sessionStart` context injection is ADDITIVE and smoke-gated (verified on cursor-agent 2026.07.23): the generated always-apply rule (.cursor/rules/harness-context.mdc, written by install.sh) is the guaranteed context path; no failClosed here because losing injection must never block a session. Each command is a LOCATOR rather than a direct call. Cursor resolves ${CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR} to ONE root, chosen when the WINDOW opened — in a multi-root window that root may be a repo with no .harness/ at all, and an unwrapped `/bin/sh <missing path>` exits 127, which failClosed turns into a deny for every edit and shell call in the session. So the locator reads the payload from stdin ONCE, resolves the repo the agent is actually touching (`git -C <payload .cwd> rev-parse --show-toplevel`, the same shape .codex/hooks.json uses), checks for .harness/ THERE, and re-emits the captured payload into .harness/adapters/cursor/dispatch.sh. ${CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR} stays as the SECOND candidate — never a replacement — so the events that carry no per-repo location (stop, sessionStart) keep working and payload text can only ADD a candidate root, never remove the anchor. No .harness/ at the resolved root means the hook does not apply (exit 0); .harness/ present but the dispatcher missing is exit 3, so a broken vendoring is loud rather than silently unenforced.

sessionStart.command: /bin/sh -c 'P=$(cat); M=$1; D=$2; shift 2; R=; for C in "$(printf '\''%s'\'' "$P" | sed -nE '\''s/.*"(cwd|file_path)"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"([^"]*)".*/\2/p'\'' | tail -1)" "${CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}"; do [ -n "$C" ] || continue; [ -d "$C" ] || C=$(dirname -- "$C"); T=$(git -C "$C" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || continue; [ -e "$T/$M" ] || continue; R=$T; break; done; [ -n "$R" ] || exit 0; [ -f "$R/$D" ] || { echo "AIOS hook: $R has the harness marker but $D is missing - refusing to run unguarded" >&2; exit 3; }; printf '\''%s'\'' "$P" | /bin/sh "$R/$D" "$R" "$@"' aios-cursor-hook .harness .harness/adapters/cursor/dispatch.sh hook session_start inject-context.sh
